title: Taylor and Maclaurin series

blocks.text: Taylor’s series about a is \(f(x)=f(a)+(x-a)f\prime(a)+(x-a)^2f^{\prime\prime}(a)/2!+\cdots\), when the remainder tends to zero. At a=0 it is Maclaurin’s series.
The finite theorem retains the Lagrange remainder \((x-a)^nf^{(n)}(a+\theta(x-a))/n!\), \(0<\theta<1\).

items.title: Standard Maclaurin expansions
question_paragraphs: Expand \(e^x,\sin x,\cos x,\sinh x\) in powers of x.
paragraphs: For \(e^x\), all derivatives at zero equal 1, giving \(e^x=1+x+x^2/2!+x^3/3!+\cdots\).
The sine derivatives cycle as sin, cos, −sin, −cos; the nonzero values at zero are \(f^{(2k+1)}(0)=(-1)^k\). Thus \(\sin x=x-x^3/3!+x^5/5!-\cdots\).

PankusDesk completion for the remaining two prompts: cosine has \(f^{(2k)}(0)=(-1)^k\), and sinh has every odd derivative equal to 1 at zero. Therefore \(\cos x=1-x^2/2!+x^4/4!-\cdots\), \(\sinh x=x+x^3/3!+x^5/5!+\cdots\).
items.final_answer: The four displayed series converge for every real x.

textbook_match.note: The standard series are listed in Text; the photographed notebook works out eˣ and sin x, and leaves cos x and sinh x as prompts.

items.title: Taylor expansion about π/4
question_paragraphs: Expand \(\sin x\) in powers of \(x-\pi/4\) through the cubic term.
paragraphs: At a=π/4 the first four derivative values are \(1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt2,-1/\sqrt2,-1/\sqrt2\).

items.title: Exponential of x sin x
question_paragraphs: Expand \(e^{x\sin x}\) in powers of x.
paragraphs: \(e^t=1+t+t^2/2+\cdots\); through degree three this is \(1+x^2+O(x^4)\), as in the notebook.
PankusDesk extension: the next coefficient is \(-1/6+1/2=1/3\), giving \(1+x^2+x^4/3+O(x^6)\).

textbook_match.note: The worked textbook example expands e^(sin x); the notebook exponent is x sin x. Problems 4.5 Q13 contains the latter series with one further term.
